title: What a ratio tells you
observableEvidence: States a ratio relationship using 'for every' or 'to' language and identifies the two quantities being compared.
explanation:
A ratio compares two quantities. A bag has 6 red marbles and 8 yellow marbles. The ratio of red marbles to yellow marbles is 6 to 8.

Ways to write it: 6:8, 6 to 8, or 6/8. All of them say "for every 6 red marbles, there are 8 yellow marbles."

Order matters. Red to yellow is 6:8, but yellow to red is 8:6. Write the quantity that is named first in the question first in the ratio.

Part-to-part and part-to-whole. Red to yellow compares one part with another part. Red to all the marbles compares one part with the whole bag. To find the whole, add the parts: 6 + 8 = 14 marbles, so red to all the marbles is 6:14. Be careful with fraction notation: 6/8 can name the red-to-yellow ratio, but red marbles are 6/14 of the bag, not 6/8 of it.

Simplest form. Divide both numbers by their greatest common factor. 6:8 becomes 3:4 after dividing both numbers by 2. It describes the same relationship: for every 3 red marbles there are 4 yellow marbles.

A ratio is not a count and not a difference. 3:4 does not mean the bag holds exactly 3 red marbles. It also does not mean there is always 1 more yellow marble than red. A bag with 12 red and 16 yellow marbles has the same ratio, 3:4, but it has 4 more yellow marbles than red. To make an equivalent ratio, multiply both numbers by the same number; adding the same amount to both numbers changes the ratio.
workedExample:
A class has 12 students who walk to school and 9 students who ride the bus. Every student does exactly one of these.
Step 1. Walkers to bus riders: 12:9. Both numbers divide by 3, so the simplest form is 4:3. For every 4 walkers there are 3 bus riders.
Step 2. Bus riders to walkers: reverse the order to get 3:4.
Step 3. Walkers to all students: the whole class is 12 + 9 = 21 students. Walkers to all students is 12:21, which simplifies to 4:7.
Check: 4 + 3 = 7, so in every group of 7 students, 4 walk and 3 ride the bus.

accessibilityNotes: Plain text only; no image, table or color carries meaning. Ratios are written with colons and also in words so a screen reader can read them either way.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A ratio compares two quantities in a stated order, for example 6 red marbles to 8 yellow marbles, written 6:8, 6 to 8 or 6/8. Reversing the order changes the ratio. Part-to-part compares two parts; part-to-whole compares a part with the total. Simplify by dividing both numbers by a common factor. Worked example: 12 walkers and 9 bus riders give 4:3, the reverse 3:4, and walkers to all 21 students 4:7.
